title: The Gift of a Free Evening
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の天体・実証結果・人物・法令ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Two friends, Aki and Lina, usually meet on Friday evenings.
sentences.ja: 友人のアキとリナはたいてい金曜の夕方に会う。

sentences.en: They enjoy talking about their experiences during the week.
sentences.ja: 一週間の経験について話すことを楽しむ。

sentences.en: One Friday, Lina sends a message saying that she would like to spend the evening alone.
sentences.ja: ある金曜、リナは一人で夕方を過ごしたいという連絡を送る。

sentences.en: Aki initially worries that Lina no longer enjoys their meetings.
sentences.ja: アキは当初、リナがもう会うことを楽しんでいないのではと心配する。

sentences.en: Instead of immediately canceling all their future plans, Aki asks whether something has changed.
sentences.ja: すぐ将来の予定を全て取り消すのでなく、何か変わったか尋ねる。

sentences.en: Lina explains that she has had an unusually demanding week and needs some time to rest.
sentences.ja: リナは非常に忙しい週を過ごし休息時間が必要だと説明する。

sentences.en: She still values their friendship and hopes to meet the following week.
sentences.ja: 友情をまだ大事にしており翌週会いたいと思っている。

sentences.en: Aki begins to recognize that a request for personal time need not indicate a loss of interest in another person.
sentences.ja: 個人時間の希望が相手への関心の喪失を示すとは限らないとアキは気づき始める。

sentences.en: The friends discuss how to communicate when their usual plans become difficult to follow.
sentences.ja: 通常予定に従うことが難しくなった時どう連絡するか話し合う。

sentences.en: They agree that it is helpful to explain a change without feeling required to provide every detail of their personal lives.
sentences.ja: 個人生活の全詳細を説明する必要を感じず変更を伝えることが役立つと同意する。

sentences.en: They also recognize that a short message sent in advance can help the other person make alternative plans.
sentences.ja: 事前の短い連絡が相手の別予定作成を助けると認識する。

sentences.en: Their arrangement allows them to continue meeting regularly while making occasional changes when necessary.
sentences.ja: 仕組みは必要な時たまに変更しながら定期的に会い続けることを可能にする。

sentences.en: The following Friday, Aki finds that she has an important task to finish at home.
sentences.ja: 翌金曜、アキは自宅で終えるべき重要な作業があることに気づく。

sentences.en: She sends Lina a message explaining the situation and suggests a different time for their meeting.
sentences.ja: 状況を説明する連絡を送り別の会合時間を提案する。

sentences.en: Lina appreciates the information and agrees to the change.
sentences.ja: リナは情報に感謝し変更に同意する。

sentences.en: Neither friend treats the revised plan as evidence that their relationship has become less important.
sentences.ja: どちらも修正予定を関係が重要でなくなった証拠とは扱わない。

sentences.en: A friendship can involve both shared experiences and respect for individual needs.
sentences.ja: 友情は共有経験と個々の必要への尊重の両方を伴い得る。

sentences.en: Maintaining a relationship does not always require keeping every arrangement unchanged.
sentences.ja: 関係維持には全ての取り決めを変更しないことが常に必要とは限らない。

sentences.en: Clear communication can help people distinguish a temporary change of plans from a change in their feelings.
sentences.ja: 明確な意思疎通は一時的予定変更と感情変化を区別する助けになり得る。

sentences.en: Sometimes giving a friend some time can be a meaningful way of expressing care.
sentences.ja: 時に友人に時間を与えることが思いやりを表す意味ある方法となり得る。

vocabulary.definition: no more at the present time
relating to time yet to come
state of no longer having something

questions.prompt: When do the friends usually meet?
Why does Lina's message worry Aki?
options: Aki is unable to read the message.
Aki thinks it may signal less interest in their friendship.
Lina wants to end their friendship explicitly.
She has moved to a different town.
She needs rest after a demanding week.
She has decided to stop speaking to Aki.
She has no free evenings in the future.

questions.prompt: What does Aki learn about personal time?
options: Friends must never spend time alone.
Every change of plans means a relationship has ended.
A request for time always indicates disagreement.
Wanting personal time does not necessarily imply less interest in a friend.
questions.explanation_ja: 個人時間と友情は両立。

questions.prompt: What communication practice do they agree on?
options: Provide a complete daily report to each other.
Explain changes without needing to reveal every personal detail.
Cancel future meetings whenever one plan changes.
questions.explanation_ja: 必要な説明とプライバシー。

questions.prompt: Why send a message in advance?
options: It allows the other friend to make different plans.
It proves no other friend is important.
It requires both people to cancel all activities.
questions.explanation_ja: 別の予定を立てられる。

options: Aki has a task to complete and suggests another meeting time.
They have decided that meetings are meaningless.
They can accept a changed plan without interpreting it as rejection.
Only Lina is allowed to change plans.
The new arrangement creates an immediate disagreement.
questions.explanation_ja: 予定変更を拒絶と見なさない。

options: Friends must follow every plan exactly.
Good communication requires revealing all personal details.
Friendship can include respecting individual time while communicating changes clearly.

grammar.focus: need not indicate a loss of interest
from a change in their feelings

paraphrases.rewrite: Aki checks if something is different instead of assuming the worst.

paraphrases.source: Aki begins to recognize that a request for personal time need not indicate a loss of interest in another person.
paraphrases.rewrite: Wanting time alone does not have to mean a friend is less important.

paraphrases.source: Their arrangement allows them to continue meeting regularly while making occasional changes when necessary.
paraphrases.rewrite: They can keep meeting while adjusting plans when needed.

paraphrases.source: Clear communication can help people distinguish a temporary change of plans from a change in their feelings.
paraphrases.rewrite: Communication helps separate a scheduling change from a change of affection.

discourse.role_ja: 一方的に取り消すのでなく確認。
状況に応じた思いやり。
